title: Fail-closed no-egress guard (per-scope local_only) + agent-discoverable egress-posture report
priority_note: The primitive that turns 'I hope it stays local' into an ENFORCED invariant. Marking data local_only and refusing, fail-closed, any outbound provider call to a non-local endpoint for that data means a private document can NEVER accidentally egress — even via a misconfig. Plus an agent-discoverable posture report so an agent can VERIFY locality before harvesting sensitive data (loopctl is agent-native, self-discoverable, no UI).

background.reference: Epic 37 added lib/loopctl/provider/admission.ex — a single chokepoint in front of EVERY outbound provider Req.post (embedding US-37.1; admission gate resolves via Loopctl.RateLimiter.Behaviour). That chokepoint is the ideal enforcement point for an egress guard. Today there is no concept of 'this data must not leave the box'.
background.includes: Add a local_only marking at the scope level (tenant and/or project, and optionally per-ingest request) + an allowlist of local/private endpoints (loopback, private ranges, or an explicit LOCAL_ENDPOINT_ALLOWLIST). At the admission chokepoint, before any provider call handling local_only data, if the resolved endpoint is not in the allowlist → refuse with {:error, :egress_blocked} (fail-closed), surfaced as a clear agent-readable error. Add an egress-posture MCP tool + endpoint reporting: configured provider endpoints, whether each is local, and per-scope local_only status.

story.as_a: an agent about to harvest a user's private documents
story.i_want_to: mark the target scope local_only and have loopctl HARD-REFUSE any provider call that would send that data to a non-local endpoint, and be able to query the instance's egress posture first
story.so_that: private data can never leave the box — not by misconfiguration, not by a wrong base_url — and I can verify the instance is fully local before I start

rationale: Config knobs (US-39.1/2/3) MAKE local possible; this GUARANTEES it. A fail-closed check at the epic-37 admission chokepoint is the cheapest place to enforce a no-egress invariant for marked data, and an egress-posture report makes locality self-discoverable — both squarely in loopctl's agent-native design. Together they convert the user's privacy 'worry' into a provable property.

acceptance_criteria.description: A local_only marking exists at scope level (at least per-tenant and/or per-project; optionally per-ingest). When set, Provider.Admission refuses any outbound provider call (embedding, extraction, classification, merge) whose resolved endpoint is not in the local/allowlisted set, returning {:error, :egress_blocked} BEFORE the Req.post. Fail-CLOSED: if the endpoint can't be classified as local, it is treated as non-local (refuse).

The local/allowlist classification is explicit and configurable: loopback + private-range hosts, plus an operator LOCAL_ENDPOINT_ALLOWLIST. api.openai.com / api.anthropic.com are never local. A test asserts a local_only scope with an OpenAI base_url is BLOCKED, and with a local base_url is ALLOWED.

egress_blocked degrades safely and legibly: the interactive path treats it like the circuit-open/rate-limited-local fallback (keyword search, never a 500); harvesting fails the item with a clear, agent-readable reason ('scope is local_only but endpoint X is not local') so the agent knows to fix config, NOT retry blindly. No data is sent.

An agent-discoverable egress-posture surface: a new MCP tool (e.g. egress_posture) + JSON endpoint reports the configured embedding/extraction endpoints, whether each is classified local, the LOCAL_ENDPOINT_ALLOWLIST, and per-scope local_only status. No secrets leaked (endpoints shown, keys never). This is how an agent verifies locality before harvesting sensitive data. NO UI (agent-native).

Default-off + non-breaking: scopes are not local_only by default; the hosted instance behaves exactly as today. Setting local_only is opt-in via API/MCP. The guard adds one cheap classification check per provider call (no measurable hot-path cost).

test_cases.name: local_only + cloud endpoint is blocked fail-closed
steps: attempt to embed/extract for that scope
expected_results: {:error, :egress_blocked}; NO Req.post to openai (mock zero); clear reason

test_cases.name: unclassifiable endpoint fails closed
preconditions: local_only=true; endpoint not in allowlist, not obviously local

test_cases.name: egress-posture report
expected_results: reports endpoints + local/non-local classification + per-scope local_only; no secrets

technical_notes: Files: lib/loopctl/provider/admission.ex (add the egress classification + fail-closed refuse), a scope local_only column (tenants and/or projects) + migration, endpoint-classification helper (loopback/private-range/allowlist), config LOCAL_ENDPOINT_ALLOWLIST, a new egress-posture controller/endpoint + MCP tool, the interactive + harvest call sites to handle :egress_blocked.
Enforce at the SINGLE admission chokepoint so every provider path (embedding + the US-39.3 extraction provider) is covered by construction — do not scatter checks.
Fail-CLOSED is the whole point: unknown/unclassifiable endpoint => non-local => refuse. Better to block a harvest than leak.
Depends on US-39.2 + US-39.3 (needs the resolved endpoints to classify). Agent-native posture report, no UI.
MCP-server change → package.json bump. Config-based DI; no Application.put_env in tests; assert outcome class not timing.
